title: Integrator Evidence Dossier — Security, Cost, and Case Studies
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This dossier is a concise, evidence-first kit for systems integrators, SI sales engineers, and partner account teams who need to accelerate technical evaluation conversations with enterprise buyers (CTO, Head of Platform, Security, and Procurement). It bundles: positioning lines, a compact competitive snapshot, defensible pricing scenarios, short case studies, a prioritized security FAQ, and an engineering integration checklist.

Audience:
- Systems Integrators and Solutions Engineers
- Partner GTM and Technical Account Managers
- Enterprise technical buyers evaluating inference platforms

How to use this pack:
1) Open with the one-page positioning brief (Section: "Key positioning lines").
2) If the prospect is cost-sensitive, lead with the Pricing Scenarios and the unit-economics calculator.
3) If the prospect is security-sensitive, surface the Security FAQ early and offer a data-room call with Security & Product.
4) For proof-of-value, propose a two-week integrator-led pilot using the implementation checklist.

Key positioning lines (one-liners to tailor to buyer persona)
- For Platform/Infrastructure leads: "Deliver predictable, sub-50ms tail latency at scale while halving token spend through workload-aware batching and KV-prefix caching."
- For Security/Compliance leads: "Run the same Redwood inference runtime in VPC or on-prem with customer-managed KMS and audit-forwarding to SIEM — we treat your tenancy and logs as first-class outputs."
- For Product/ML leads: "Ship model rollouts and rollback policies with per-route tracing and quality guards; iterate on prompts without risking production regressions."
- For Procurement/Finance: "Reserved Dedicated capacity gives you predictable unit costs — we provide the math and conservatively estimate a 30–45% TCO reduction vs unmanaged GPU fleet rebuilds on 6–12 month horizons."

Competitive snapshot (1-page matrix)
- Table: (columns: Capability / Redwood / Leading Managed API / Self‑Hosted Open Runtime)
  - Production SLOs: Redwood: SLA-backed latency targets + canary rollouts; Managed API: best-effort; Self-hosted: varies by team
  - Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): Redwood: Supported + integration playbook; Managed API: usually no; Self-hosted: yes (but heavy ops)
  - Cost controls (batching/caching/quantization): Redwood: built-in Optimize toolkit + model profiles; Managed API: limited; Self-hosted: possible, engineering heavy
  - Observability & tracing: Redwood: token-level, per-route dashboards; Managed API: aggregate metrics; Self-hosted: depends on instrumentation
  - Enterprise support & onboarding: Redwood: SI onboarding playbook + partner engineering; Managed API: support tiers; Self-hosted: professional services required

Competitive positioning talking points:
- Against managed API incumbents: emphasize economics controls (batching + caching) and predictable reserved capacity options.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize time-to-production, operational hygiene, and integrated rollouts + fallback policies.

Pricing guidance and example scenarios
- Pricing constructs we use: per-token generation units, per-embedding unit, hourly reserved capacity (Dedicated), and professional services for Private deployments.
- Example scenario A — Customer-facing chat bot (moderate throughput):
  * 5M generation tokens / month, 2M embedding units / month.
  * Hosted with Redwood: blended unit price -> estimated monthly cost = $3,800 (illustrative).
  * Dedicated commitment (6 GPU equivalent) -> monthly commitment = $22,000, estimated unit cost reduction 40% at sustained load; break-even vs hosted at ~9 months depending on utilization.
- Example scenario B — Regulated financial institution (sensitive data, on-prem):
  * On-prem subscription: platform license + annual support. Typical first-year TCO includes packaging & professional services: license $120k, PS $75k, HW ops incremental cost $50k. Value: full control over data residency, audit log pipeline integration.

Unit-economics checklist for customer conversations:
1) Collect expected peak RPS and median request length (tokens in + tokens out).
2) Identify SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency targets) and acceptable tail latency.
3) Determine security posture (hosted/dedicated/private).
4) Run model profile (we can provide a quick perf profile within 48h) to estimate token / GPU-second rates.
5) Present Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with month 1 and steady-state 12-month numbers.

Case studies (two compact, integrator-friendly narratives)
- Case study: InsurTech claims automation (partner integration)
  * Problem: Latency spikes caused poor UX on claims triage; cost was unpredictable under burst loads.
  * Approach: Integrator ran a 3-week pilot using Redwood Dedicated, enabled prefix caching for repeated question templates, and configured auto-scale burst capacity for seasonal peaks.
  * Outcome: 55% reduction in per-conversation token cost, 40% lower p95 latency, and the customer moved to an annual Dedicated contract.
- Case study: Healthcare document ingestion (on-prem + compliance)
  * Problem: PHI-sensitive processing required on-prem inference with strict audit trails.
  * Approach: Redwood Private deployed with HSM-backed KMS integration and audit-forwarding to Splunk; SI handled network zoning and airgap checklist.
  * Outcome: Compliance audit passed, deployment accepted for production in 8 weeks, customer cited strong observability and rollout controls as key decision factors.

Security FAQ (prioritized, short answers to use in sales calls)
1) Q: Can Redwood run entirely inside our VPC or air-gapped environment?
   A: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control plane and a packaged on-prem runtime. We have an air-gap deployment checklist and offer professional services to validate network zoning.
2) Q: How is customer data isolated from other tenants?
   A: Each Dedicated or Private deployment uses tenant-isolated compute with separate model caches and KV namespaces. Hosted plans logically isolate customer data and we offer Dedicated for full compute isolation.
3) Q: Where are logs and telemetry sent? Can we forward to our SIEM?
   A: We stream audit logs and traces to your endpoints (S3, Splunk, Datadog, etc.) and provide structured audit events for every request.
4) Q: What KMS/HSM integrations do you support?
   A: We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs via PKCS#11 adapters for Private installs.
5) Q: Do you perform penetration tests and provide evidence?
   A: Yes — we run annual third-party pentests and can provide executive summaries under NDA; for enterprise deals we share SOC2 Type II and selected test artifacts in the security data room.
6) Q: How does Redwood minimize model-regression risks during rollouts?
   A: Built-in canary rollouts, A/B testing, prompt-set based quality monitors, and regression alerts tied to evals; we can gate rollouts on prompt set pass rates.

Integration & pilot checklist (recommended 10-step integrator flow)
1) Pre-sales: Collect business objective, SLOs, data residency, and pilot success metrics.
2) Connectivity: Provide network allowlist + certs for secure control plane traffic.
3) Perf profile: Run a quick 48h model profile to size GPU needs.
4) Pilot environment: Provision a short-lived Dedicated or Private sandbox.
5) Observability hook-up: Configure log export (Splunk/Datadog) and set up per-route dashboards.
6) Cost controls: Enable batching and KV-prefix caching; select quantization profile if acceptable.
7) Security review: Exchange architecture diagram; run SI threat checklist.
8) Functional validation: Run the pre-agreed prompt set and quality evals.
9) Load validation: Simulate peak RPS for 2 hours and verify SLOs.
10) Close: Collect metrics, prepare renewal/scale plan, and move to contract.

Pitch deck slide outline (15 slides, quick narrative)
1) Title / customer logo
2) Executive summary: business outcome and ask
3) Why inference economics matter (latency + unit cost)
4) Redwood one-liner + deployment modes
5) Architecture: Hosted / Dedicated / Private options
6) Observability and rollouts (screenshots)
7) Cost control levers & Optimize toolkit
8) Security & compliance (KMS, audit, pentest evidence)
9) Pilot approach & timeline (2–6 weeks)
10) Case studies (2 slides)
11) Pricing scenarios & break-even math
12) Integration checklist & responsibilities
13) SLA and support model
14) Commercial ask and next steps
15) Contacts and data-room link

Redwood playbook tips for integrators (do/don't)
- Do: Lead with measurable success metrics (cost per convo, p95 latency) rather than abstract features.
- Do: Ask for a 48-hour profiling window early — it converts budget conversations into engineering decisions.
- Don't: Offer unsupported on-prem promises. Use the Private deployment checklist and engage Product Security early.

- Audit log sample (JSON event line)

Notes and next steps:
- For any prospect that requires SOC2 / pentest artifacts, open an NDA and route to Security (Leah Rivera).
- Recommended internal follow-up: run the 48h profiler within 72 hours of interest confirmation.
